snippets.output: Short-term insomnia can be effectively managed with various treatment options, including pharmacologic and non-pharmacologic solutions.
Zolpidem is a non-benzodiazepine hypnotic agent that can be effective as a pharmacologic treatment for short-term insomnia, including middle-of-the-night insomnia.
Pharmacologic treatments for short-term insomnia include hypnotics such as zolpidem, eszopiclone, and zaleplon, although their use is limited by residual daytime sedation.

CBT-I, which stands for cognitive-behavioral therapy for insomnia, is a non-pharmacologic treatment that can be effective for short-term insomnia. CBT-I is also recommended as the first-line treatment for chronic insomnia.

Non-pharmacologic treatments for short-term insomnia include sleep hygiene, such as establishing a consistent sleep schedule, avoiding caffeine and electronics before bedtime, and creating a sleep-conducive environment.

Non-pharmacologic short-term solutions for insomnia include relaxation techniques such as progressive muscle relaxation, deep breathing, and mindfulness meditation. These techniques can reduce stress, which can make it easier to fall asleep.

A short-term solution for insomnia can be a combination of pharmacologic and non-pharmacologic treatments, such as a short course of zolpidem to help alleviate acute symptoms, along with practicing sleep hygiene and relaxation techniques to address underlying sleep habits and reduce stress.
